data.summary: F10 stoppages are driven primarily by missing-part andon events and part-shortage incidents, with equipment and torque faults as secondary contributors and recurring M-06 machine failures.

findings.claim: Missing-part andon events stop the F10 line most frequently, with 97 line stops on shift A and 60 on shift B out of 208 and 145 events respectively.
Part shortage incidents create the largest downtime, led by supplier_short on shift A with 423.7 min downtime and 338 cars lost.
Torque faults are the next biggest incident downtime source, with controller_fault on shift A totaling 272.0 min downtime and 216 cars lost.
Equipment andon events also halt production often, causing 65 line stops on shift A and 66 on shift B.
Telemetry shows machine M-06 repeatedly fails, including overstrain failures, with tool wear peaking at 189.7 min on 2026-09-13.

data.recommendation: Address F10 stoppages first by securing supplier parts and AGV availability, then implement preventive maintenance on M-06 to reduce overstrain failures and tool wear.
